content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Use step/job outputs for small structured values and artifacts for files; a new job should not assume that another job’s runner filesystem is shared. Artifacts preserve files produced by a run; caches accelerate reconstruction of dependencies. They serve different purposes and neither should contain secrets. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Step outputs
items.text: Write one step output as `name=value` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, then declare job outputs if a downstream job needs the value. Use `$GITHUB_ENV` for values needed by later steps in the same job.

items.title: Job outputs
items.text: Write one step output as `name=value` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, then declare job outputs if a downstream job needs the value. Use `$GITHUB_ENV` for values needed by later steps in the same job.

items.title: The needs context
items.text: Declare job dependencies with `needs` and read prerequisite results or outputs through `needs.<job>`. Separate jobs do not share a runner workspace automatically.

items.title: Artifact-based data transfer
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

items.title: Choosing outputs versus artifacts
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

items.title: Avoiding assumptions about shared runner filesystems
items.text: Choose runner labels and access boundaries that match the workload. Self-hosted machines need patching, network segmentation, secret protection, and cleanup; keep untrusted contributions away from privileged persistent runners.

content_blocks.code:
name: Pass a small value between jobs
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      label: ${{ steps.make.outputs.label }}
    steps:
      - id: make
        run: echo "label=demo-${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  consume:
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          LABEL: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.label }}
        run: echo "Received label=$LABEL"
content_blocks.expected_output: The prepare job exports a small string as a job output; the dependent job consumes that string through `needs.prepare.outputs.label`. Outputs are not a file-transfer mechanism.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a test repository or static validation first. Confirm the secret/variable scope and permissions match your environment before a real run.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain sharing data between jobs, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Choose between short-lived outputs, persisted artifacts, and reusable dependency caches.

troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
